data.name: PbrMaterials_Intro
data.value: Three spheres wearing real-world materials from Poly Haven (CC0): rusted iron sheet (rust is a dielectric, only the exposed metal spots read metallic — the ARM blue channel is mottled), a mixed brick wall (a rough dielectric dominated by its normal map), and a galvanized sheet (metal ≈ 0.9, roughness ≈ 0.13, with a sharp IBL reflection). Each material is three maps: diff → BaseColor, nor_gl → Normal, arm → MetallicRoughness (R = AO, G = roughness, B = metallic — exactly the glTF packing, no channel shuffling needed).

data.name: PbrMaterials_Note
data.value: The skybox behind them is not just backdrop: metals have no diffuse term, so without the IBL built from this cube map a metal sphere is a dull grey blob. The ambient term is dialed down to 0.45 here so the sun highlights and shadows keep the three regimes apart. Textures are 1024 px JPEG, ~2.9 MB total, downloaded on page entry.

data.name: Demo_PointcloudMix_Summary
data.value: A procedural point cloud and a glTF table in one default pipeline: point size, unlit and vertex colors are plain material parameters — no shader overrides, and the pipeline stays switchable

data.name: PointcloudMix_Intro
data.value: The rainbow shell is a 6000-point cloud (xyz + rgb, exactly what a .ply carries) hovering over a glTF table, both drawn by the default pipeline. Point size, unlit and vertex colors are ordinary material parameters: the engine writes gl_PointSize for point primitives, falls back to a stable normal when the cloud has none, and the loader applies the same preset to xyz/rgb .ply files. Switch the pipeline at the bottom — the same scene keeps rendering. Turn unlit off to see why point clouds default to it: shading with the fallback normal goes dark on the wrong side.

data.name: AnimationMix_Intro
data.value: The two characters share one skeleton and each shows a way of combining several clips into a pose: left is the state machine (AnimationGraph) — idle/walk/run are three discrete states, and switching crossfades over BlendTime; right is the blend space (AnimationBlendSpace) — six clips sit at six points on a plane and the pose interpolates continuously by (X, Y) axis values. Left shows switching, right shows blending.

data.name: AnimationMix_TransitionNote
data.value: Transition predicates are queried every frame but only checked once CurrentWeight reaches 1 (the previous fade-in has finished), so lengthening BlendTime makes switches noticeably sluggish. AddNextNode also forbids a node pointing at itself: to loop you need two nodes pointing at each other.

data.name: AnimationMix_AutoSweep
data.value: Sweep forward automatically (idle → walk → run → idle)

data.name: AnimationMix_BlendSpaceNote
data.value: The rectangle above is a top-down view of the 2D blend space; both axes run from -1 to +1. On the vertical axis: top = run forward, halfway = walk forward, bottom = walk backwards (KayKit has no backward run); on the horizontal axis: left/right ends = strafe runs; the origin = idle. The six grey dots are the sample clips and the blue thumb is the current axis value — drag it and the right character instantly plays the blended pose at those weights. With auto sweep on, the thumb shuttles up and down the vertical axis by itself; dragging manually pauses the sweep until you re-enable the toggle. Higher IdwPower hugs the nearest sample.

data.name: AssimpFbx_Intro
data.value: SK_Mannequin.FBX carries no animation; the motion lives in two separate FBX files. A single file may contain several clips, and both the count and the names are read from the file itself.

data.name: AssimpFbx_NoSamplerNote
data.value: Choosing "no sampler" leaves Model.AnimationSampler null, so drawing falls back to Skeleton.BoneMatrixBuffer (the bind pose) and the character returns to T-pose — this is the line `mesh.AnimationSampler?.BoneMatrixBuffer ?? mesh.Skeleton!.BoneMatrixBuffer` inside the render pass.

data.name: AssimpFbx_AtSecond
data.value: Sample at which second of the clip

data.name: AssimpFbx_SampleNote
data.value: Animation.Sample(channel name, seconds) returns that bone's matrix at that moment. The engine has no player with a Play method — the player is hand-written: AnimationSampler advances time frame by frame and calls Sample. The slider pins that time for it.

data.name: Background_Intro
data.value: There is a single entry point for backgrounds: Scene.Background, typed OneOf<CubeTexture, Texture>. The cubemap branch samples by view direction, so the sky follows camera rotation only, not translation (the view the pass computes is a LookAt centred on the origin) — orbit with the right mouse button, then walk with WASD to separate the two. The plain-texture branch draws a window-filling quad, stretched rather than equirectangularly mapped, and does not move at all when you orbit.

data.name: Background_CubeSize
data.value: Cubemap edge length when baking the HDRI

data.name: Background_ClearNote
data.value: Turning this off gives a solid black frame, not a checkerboard: BackgroundPass.BeforeRender clears to (0,0,0,0) unconditionally and the early-out happens inside Render, so this switch governs whether the background is drawn, not whether the clear happens.

data.name: Background_Orthographic
data.value: Orthographic projection (takes the SKYBOX + ORTHOGRAPHIC branch)

data.name: Background_ProjectionNote
data.value: The two variants source their framing differently, so the three sliders behave asymmetrically. The perspective branch recomputes its own projection from FOV with near/far hardcoded to 10..100, so FOV changes the sky framing while FarPlane does nothing. The orthographic branch uses the camera's own projection matrix, but the fragment's framing extent is hardcoded to 100 times the aspect ratio and never reads OrthographicSize, so changing OrthographicSize only scales the foreground while changing FarPlane scales the sky. Scrolling does nothing under orthographic either: zoom works by moving the eye, and a parallel frustum is independent of eye position. Both hardcodings are engine inconsistencies, not misuse. The projection parameters themselves, FitToBoundingBox and WorldToScreen included, have their own demo on the camera page.

data.name: Background_KeyLightVisible
data.value: Directional light visible (turn off to light with IBL only)

data.name: Background_RebakeIbl
data.value: Rebake IBL (switching sources already rebakes; for in-place content changes)

data.name: Background_IblNote
data.value: Irradiance and prefiltered reflections only recognise the cubemap branch: when Background is not a CubeTexture they fall back to the engine's default cube (IrradianceMapPass reads RenderPipeline.DefaultIblAmbientCubeTexture). Both results are cached on the camera node and reused whenever FrameBufferId is non-zero, so flipping between the four sources on this page leaves the sphere's reflections unchanged — press the button above to Invalidate, or Reload. The full caching demo lives on the ibl-environment page.

data.name: Camera_Intro
data.value: Orthographic projection has no near-large-far-small, which makes it the right tool for measuring; changing FieldOfView under perspective alters both the vertical field and the effective aspect. Pulling near and far apart so they straddle an object reveals a cross-section — a second kind of invisibility on top of frustum culling.

data.name: CelShading_Intro
data.value: Cel shading is the only pipeline in the engine that consumes material parameters by name: six channel names plus a list of underscore-prefixed float/Vector4. A typo never raises an error, the value simply has no effect and the built-in default applies — the pass pre-loads every uniform with the reference cel material (from the historical Nilou character), so a material with missing parameters or textures still renders normally.

data.name: CelShading_DarkFac
data.value: _DarkFac: NDotL offset (pushes the shadow side up)

data.name: CelShading_BrightFac
data.value: _BrightFac: lit threshold (above it the raw halfLambert is used)

data.name: CelShading_RampRowsNote
data.value: The row coordinate is computed as 1.05 - 0.1*index - 0.5, and that trailing 0.5 comes from _UseCoolShadowColorOrTex, which is hardcoded to 1 (night) on the C# side — so the five values below are the only way to move the sampled row. The built-in ramp has two rows; a ramp of your own needs five before it is useful (this page generates one).

data.name: CelShading_CoolShadowNote
data.value: The cool slot is the dark colour the body and face actually use: _UseCoolShadowColorOrTex is always 1, so mix(_DarkShadowColor, _CoolDarkShadowColor, 1) discards the warm slot outright. Dragging the middle slider to 0 will not go black — the one that matters is below it.

data.name: CelShading_FaceRenderType
data.value: RenderType=1 with the face tag (takes the FACE_RENDER branch)

data.name: CelShading_OutlineNote
data.value: This is OutlinePass's only public knob. Outline width and colour are private fields (2f / 1.5f / black), and the pass instance can only be found by type in RenderPipeline.EveryCameraRenderPasses, which is exactly how this page gets it.

data.name: Environment_Intro
data.value: Irradiance and prefiltered reflections are each baked once and parked in two GPU-state slots on the camera node, then reused every frame. Assigning a new Background notifies the pipeline (OnBackgroundChanged), which invalidates both caches automatically - the next frame rebakes from the new map, so switching environments needs no manual step. The rebake button covers the remaining case: the resource reference stayed the same but its content changed in place, or you want to force a recomputation - it calls Invalidate() to zero the frame buffers.

data.name: Environment_FaceSizeNote
data.value: Edge length only applies to the panorama branches (HDRI and procedural): it is the bake target. Picking the six-face skybox feeds that cube straight to IBL, so the edge length comes from those images and this slider is inert.

data.name: Environment_Reload
data.value: Reload the page (also needed when switching pipelines)

data.name: Environment_BackgroundNote
data.value: Background is OneOf<CubeTexture, Texture>: only the cubemap branch drives IBL, a plain texture is just drawn as the backdrop. With no cubemap set the PBR pipelines do not skip IBL — they fall back to PBRPipelineBase.DefaultIblAmbientCubeTexture, which is a 16px cube converted from Texture.CreateFromColor(White). Flat white means the ambient term has no direction and the prefiltered reflection has no shape: metal turns into an evenly lit blob instead of mirroring its surroundings. Only a cubemap with actual content makes IBL readable, which is why the file-based options at the top of this page exist.

data.name: Environment_KeyLightVisible
data.value: Directional light visible (turn off to light with IBL only)

data.name: Geometries_Intro
data.value: The four shapes stand side by side, and each parameter section rebuilds its own shape's vertex data on every change — they never interfere. The dropdown only picks which shape the readout below counts vertices and indices for. The rotation speed spins the whole row about Y, which is how you inspect back-face culling and light direction.

data.name: GpuLifecycle_Intro
data.value: Every button in the upper half touches real GPU resources. GL calls may only run inside a render callback, so these APIs merely queue requests and the actual work happens at the start of the next frame — you can see that in the event ordering.

data.name: GpuLifecycle_ReleaseGpu
data.value: ReleaseGpuResources(): drop the GL objects, keep the scene

data.name: GpuLifecycle_SimulateLost
data.value: SimulateContextLost(): mark the handle dead, rebuild on the next frame

data.name: GpuLifecycle_OnDemandNote
data.value: With continuous rendering off, the picture freezes on the current frame: orbiting the camera or dragging a slider triggers no repaint, because the camera controller only moves the camera. That is why on-demand rendering has to own every input path — the convention in this shell is to call Context.InvalidateRender() after changing scene parameters.

data.name: Hism_Intro
data.value: The octree is built on a background thread and the groups are attached as children only once it finishes, so dragging the instance count first shows IsBuilding=true. Teleporting across the field moves an instance to a different leaf and rebuilds the whole tree; stepping it a short way only rewrites the buffer of its own group — an order of magnitude apart in cost.

data.name: Instancing_Intro
data.value: Both fields hold the same instance count; the right one uses per-instance vertex colours. Its vertex shader carries an INSTANCED_MESH branch, so one material serves both a plain Mesh (uniform branch) and an InstancedMesh (attribute branch). Per-instance attribute arrays must be exactly the instance count long, so this page always creates the instances before attaching the attributes.

data.name: Instancing_RemoveInstances
data.value: RemoveInstance: drop the first 200 in the left field

data.name: MaterialShaders_Intro
data.value: Custom shaders attach to a material keyed by pass class name (this page overrides LightPass throughout), and you can replace the fragment stage alone while keeping the engine's vertex stage. Material parameters bind to same-named uniforms. Note: writing a parameter raises the material's Version and forces materials carrying custom shaders to recompile, which is why per-frame uniform writes are off by default.

data.name: MaterialShaders_WriteTime
data.value: Write uTime every frame (triggers recompiles, watch the readout)

data.name: ModelViewer_Intro
data.value: The three dropdown entries marked fetch-on-entry are downloaded in one go by LoadAssetsAsync (about 3 MB on this page), so switching between them triggers no download — it only changes which Model node is enabled. The four marked in-page on demand are fetched from the page itself: they download and decode only when selected, so they are not part of the fetch-on-entry download. Keeping the heavy models in that tier means the first screen pays only for the first screen's bytes.

data.name: ModelViewer_CustomBox
data.value: CustomBoundingBox (a box larger than the model)

data.name: ModelViewer_BoxNote
data.value: These two properties are not decoration: a mesh's bounding box asks Model.CustomBoundingBox first and falls back to the geometry's, and both grow outward whenever BoundingBoxPadding is above zero. Frustum culling and the debug wireframe both use that box.

data.name: ModelViewer_CloneNote
data.value: The two clones move to either side and each can be positioned independently; the second swaps its BaseColor for a conspicuous checker texture. If the original model changes texture too, the material is still the same instance — the bluntest way to locate the sharing boundary.

data.name: ModelViewer_LoadHint
data.value: None of the four on-demand models has been fetched yet: pick one in the dropdown above to download it

data.name: Particles_Intro
data.value: Rate, lifetime and gravity take effect immediately; MaxParticles and Looping/Duration are only read on a fresh Play, because Play allocates the particle array by MaxParticles and picks between the billboard buffer and an InstancedMesh depending on whether Mesh is set.

data.name: Particles_FlipbookNote
data.value: Which frame the flipbook shows is computed per particle from its own age ratio (vAgeRatio times tiles squared), not from global time, so a single instant can display different frames out of 64 at once and the flame reads as a gradient from fresh to old. The tile count must match the sheet's real layout: setting 4 treats the top-left quarter of an 8x8 sheet as the whole image and cuts a four-frame collage. PARTICLE_FLIPBOOK is a shader macro, but the pass selects the variant per emitter every frame, so toggling it here needs no Reload.

data.name: Picking_Intro
data.value: Clicking the view fires its ObjectPicked event, which returns only the nearest hit. Turning on the centre ray picks from the middle of the viewport every frame and lists every hit at that point — the occluder is translucent but still sits in front, which is exactly the difference between the full hit list and the nearest hit.

data.name: Pipelines_Intro
data.value: Each of the five objects feeds exactly one kind of information, so whether a pipeline reads it is easy to see. A few patterns recur: - NoLight looks at no lights at all, and ignores Normal and MetallicRoughness. - Blinn-Phong reads only BaseColor and Normal; the other three PBR maps go unrecognised. - Cel adds its own ILM/ShadowRamp and an outline pass on top of the Blinn-Phong channels. - Both PBR pipelines read all five maps and need Scene.Background to supply an environment map before any IBL ambient light exists.

data.name: PostProcessing_Intro
data.value: Everything in the upper half applies per frame: the shader re-reads those uniforms every frame. The lower half changes shader variants or texture sizes and only a full page rebuild honours them — press the button, do not expect the sliders.

data.name: PostProcessing_CsmCascadeCount
data.value: CsmCascadeCount (max 4; whether the pipeline uses CSM is another matter)

data.name: Primitives_Intro
data.value: All seven primitives share one vertex set and differ only in how the GPU connects it. Changing columns, rows or amplitude genuinely rebuilds the vertex buffer; focusing one primitive moves the rest off-screen so you can read its connection rule on its own.

data.name: SceneGizmos_Intro
data.value: The wireframe reuses the main view's depth buffer, so earlier solids can occlude it; the axes are the only exception (depth testing is temporarily disabled while they draw). The hidden box with Enable=false neither renders nor draws a bounding box, which makes it the control case for how visibility is judged.

data.name: SceneGizmos_LightOrbit
data.value: Orbit speed of the two lights (deg/s)

data.name: Shadows_Intro
data.value: Cascades apply to the key directional light only. The key light is whichever light is explicitly set as Scene.MainDirectionalLight, or else the first enabled light that casts shadows. The four ShadowConfig values are used only on the single orthographic map path: a non-key light, a pipeline without CSM, or a cascade count of 1.

data.name: Shadows_KeyNote
data.value: Unchecking this hands the key light role to whichever light is auto-picked, and the two lights on this page swap positions — cascades follow the key light only, so shadow quality changes visibly.

data.name: Shadows_ConfigNote
data.value: ShadowConfig belongs to each light individually; both lights here are given the same values, so the effect stays visible when the key light falls onto the single-map path. The orthographic frame is centred on the light's origin: too small and it clips the columns, too large and every pixel covers more ground at the same resolution, so the edges soften.

data.name: Shadows_FarPlane
data.value: Camera FarPlane (sets the cascade split range)

data.name: Shadows_CsmLiveNote
data.value: Cascade count, split and resolution all apply per frame: ShadowMapPass compares CsmShadowData's resolution and cascade count every frame and rebuilds the texture array on the spot when they differ. The one exception is crossing between 1 and 2 — ENABLE_CSM is a shader define, so that step needs the Reload button below.

data.name: Shadows_WasmNote
data.value: On the browser (wasm) host the cascade count always reads 0: the cascade shadow map is a depth texture array, allocating it calls glTexImage3D, and that signature is absent from the .NET browser runtime's native table — hitting it aborts the whole runtime — so the engine forces the single orthographic map on that host. What this page shows in a browser is the single-map path, not cascades.

data.name: Shadows_LimitNote
data.value: ShadowMapPass enumerates the shadow-casting lights in DirectionalLights order and breaks as soon as the limit is passed, so dropping it to 1 leaves only the first light in the list with a shadow map, regardless of whether it is the key light.

data.name: SkinnedAnimation_Intro
data.value: Clip names and durations come from the glb's actual animations array, not from constants: this model carries four, and the TPose one is exactly what you need to check the bind pose against.

data.name: SkinnedAnimation_DriveNote
data.value: Model.Update contains a single statement: the sampler is advanced only when it is non-null and ExternalUpdate is false. Checking it hands control back to this page, and the button below feeds a fixed step — the skeleton holds still, which is the evidence for that early-out branch.

data.name: SkinnedAnimation_Attachment
data.value: Attach a BoneAttachment (a torch bound to the hand)

data.name: SkinnedAnimation_AttachNote
data.value: A BoneAttachment's WorldTransform is LocalOffset times that bone's BonesTransform times the mesh's world matrix — the same data DebugDrawPass uses to draw the bone lines — and it must sit under the scene root to be updated every frame. Turn on NormalizeScale to attach props in world units when the model root carries a global scale.
